input.rationale: Submitted the sharper variant probe (owner commits X, its Commit reaches one live peer, then a replica that holds no command recovers the instance) and recorded a second mechanism it exposed: a prepare reply that reports COMMITTED is adopted into lb.status on the pre-accept path, after which the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 discards every later reply, so the leader's own phase-1 proposal never reaches its fast quorum. A new source range and a new question cover that stall.

investigations.question: Does a recovery that restarts phase 1 from a replica without the command stall when one of its acceptors reports the instance as COMMITTED, because adopting that status makes the leader discard every later pre-accept reply?
investigations.hypothesis: The restarted phase-1 leader adopts Status COMMITTED from the first reply whose VBallot is high enough, after which the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 rejects the remaining replies, so preAcceptOKs never reaches FastQuorumSize-1 and neither the fast nor the slow commit branch is entered; the proposal stays PREACCEPTED, the instance is not completed, and the executor's retry repeats the same sequence because the peer still reports COMMITTED.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the restarted phase-1 leader's instance remains non-committed while its own emitted PreAccept received a reply set that includes a COMMITTED status, and whether a repeated startRecoveryForInstance reproduces the identical sequence (same ballots, same adopted status, no accept or commit message).

knowledge.statement: In handlePreAcceptReply the block at epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 overwrites lb.ballot, lb.cmds, lb.status, lb.seq and lb.deps whenever a reply's VBallot is >= the running lb.ballot, so a reply whose Status is COMMITTED replaces lb.status with COMMITTED; the guard immediately before it (epaxos/epaxos.go:870) returns for any reply while lb.status is neither PREACCEPTED nor PREACCEPTED_EQ, so every later reply to the same PreAccept is discarded and lb.preAcceptOKs stops increasing.
knowledge.conditions: A phase-1 proposal whose acceptor set includes a replica that already has the instance COMMITTED (or a recoverer that adopted such a status), as happens when a recovery is restarted from sub-case 6 by a replica that lacks the value while another replica has it committed (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895, 1236-1313).

scope.description: Variant of the value-adoption harness that first lets the instance owner commit the value X and then fail, so that the same instance is recovered by a replica that holds no command while another live replica holds X committed. Sequence: replica 1's conflicting premise; owner replica 0 proposes X on (0,0); replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails; replica 2's reply makes the owner enter the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3, of which replica 3 never pre-accepted the command; both AcceptReplies are delivered, so the owner COMMITS X (status COMMITTED) and broadcasts Commit - the harness delivers that Commit only to replica 2 (the first live peer in the owner's preferred order) and then fails the owner; replica 3 then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and the quiescent exchange is completed.
assumptions: Same construction, row sizing, transport boundary and crash model as the value-adoption experiment (in-process replicas, marshaled RPC structs decoded per delivery, FIFO per link, no delivery to crashed replicas).
The owner's Commit reaching only replica 2 models the owner failing immediately after the first Commit of its broadcast, which is a permitted crash point.
No production logic is modified; the authority and crash flags are set only through the target's own fields and handlers.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept/handleAcceptReply path for the owner's commit, delivers the owner's Commit to replica 2 only, fails the owner, then calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at replica 3 and delivers the resulting Prepare/PrepareReply and PreAccept traffic through the target's own handlers, recording each replica's instance state before and after.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of an instance that a peer reports as COMMITTED must not replace that value, and the recovering leader's phase-1 proposal must still be able to reach its quorum.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's adoption of a reply's Status into lb.status together with the guard that discards later replies (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895) and its value adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313); the peer's report of COMMITTED is the target's own honest reply.

comparisons.description: The value the recovery proposes does not replace the value the quorum reports; violated when the recovery's PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although a reply carried X with status COMMITTED.

The recovering replica's own instance reaches a decided state after the recovered proposal; violated when it remains in a pre-accept state because the adopted COMMITTED status made the leader discard the replies it needed.

investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

gaps.question: Does a permitted execution produce a recovery coordinator that knows instance (A, i) (crtInstance[A] >= i) but holds no command for it, so that the fabricated self-reply decides the adopted value? Candidate: an Accept-phase broadcast to a different peer set than the PreAccept broadcast (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts at the leader) lets a replica learn the instance with Status NONE and Cmds nil.

investigations.question: Can a recovering replica that is not the master-designated leader recover an instance whose accepted value sits at a ballot above its own recovery ballot, or does the periodic retry repeat the same rejected prepare with no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives every non-designated replica a fixed recovery ballot (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise), so a recovery whose accepting peers have a higher stored bal is rejected on every attempt: each reply returns before the quorum append, no sub-case is dispatched, no further message is emitted, and the periodic retry repeats the identical Prepare ballot; only r.IsLeader (set by the master's BeTheLeader RPC) lets the ballot climb above maxRecvBallot, after which the same call joins the higher ballot and reaches the sub-case dispatch.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while every matching reply carries the peers' higher stored bal and the replica emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit for that instance, and whether invoking the target's own BeTheLeader then produces a Prepare ballot above maxRecvBallot that the peers join (producing a matching reply and a dispatched sub-case).

history.question: Can a recovering replica that is not the master-designated leader recover an instance whose accepted value sits at a ballot above its own recovery ballot, or does the periodic retry repeat the same rejected prepare with no enabled repair?
history.hypothesis: makeBallot gives a fixed ballot per replica (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise) and climbs above maxRecvBallot only while r.IsLeader is true; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the master's BeTheLeader RPC sets it, so for every other replica a prepare at its fixed ballot is rejected by any acceptor whose stored bal is higher, and the three nack repairs (handlePreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply, handlePrepareReply) are all gated on r.IsLeader. executeCommands re-enqueues the same instance every COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, so the same rejected prepare is repeated without a ballot advance, and instances that depend on the stuck instance cannot execute.
history.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while the acceptors' replies all report a higher stored ballot, with no higher-ballot Prepare emitted and the instance uncommitted; and whether the same call on a replica with IsLeader true emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot.

knowledge.statement: startRecoveryForInstance places the recovering replica's own state into lb.prepareReplies as a PrepareReply whose VBallot is the newly tried recovery ballot (inst.vbal is overwritten with lb.lastTriedBallot), while its Status/Command come from the recovering replica's own instance, which for a replica that never pre-accepted is Status NONE with Cmds nil.
knowledge.conditions: Any call to startRecoveryForInstance (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1168), including calls made from executeCommands for uncommitted instances up to crtInstance[q] after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

knowledge.statement: handlePrepareReply adopts a reply's Command/Seq/Deps/Status only when reply.VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, starting from lb.ballot = the pre-recovery local vbal and evaluating the coordinator's own self-reply first; replies whose VBallot is below that running value leave lb.cmds/lb.status unchanged. lb.status == NONE then selects sub-case 6, which calls startPhase1 with state.NOOP() because lb.cmds is nil (only the self-reply's value would have replaced it).
knowledge.conditions: Recovery of instance (replica, instance) by a replica whose own state has no pre-accepted command, when all remote replies carry a value ballot below the coordinator's freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313).

knowledge.statement: In handlePrepareReply a reply whose Ballot differs from lb.lastTriedBallot increments lb.nacks and returns before the reply is appended to lb.prepareReplies, and the sub-case dispatch is guarded by len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize(); the only repair on the nack path (makeBallot plus a fresh bcastPrepare) is executed only while r.IsLeader is true. When every answering peer reports a higher stored ballot, the appended count stays at the recovering replica's own self reply, so no sub-case is selected and no PreAccept, Accept or Commit is emitted for that instance.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery where the replicas that answer the Prepare have a stored bal above the recovering replica's fixed tried ballot, so every answer is a rejection rather than a matching-ballot reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235, with epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 and 1216-1235).

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.
InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE (10M); only instances 0..2 are used, so no code path indexes beyond the allocated row.

The auxiliary broadcast of replica 1's conflicting proposal is discarded; only its local conflict state (conflicts[2][key 1]) is used as the premise that makes the leader's pre-accept reply non-equal and therefore forces the Accept phase.

Crashes are modelled as: the replica stops consuming messages, no further message is delivered to it, and every other replica's Alive flag for it is cleared, matching the target's mechanism for deciding broadcast recipients.
Replica 3's recovery is invoked through startRecoveryForInstance, the same function the target's executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD.
excluded: No client connection path, no execution of the state machine, no recovery timer loop, and no master/BeTheLeader designation (IsLeader stays false, as epaxos.New sets it).

basis.prefix: The harness builds five in-process replicas, injects the conflicting premise at replica 1, runs replica 0's proposal of X through the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, crashes replicas 1 and 0, then calls replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers the resulting Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through the package's own handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply. Every outgoing message is decoded from the bytes SendMsg flushed, so message content, ballot fields and commands are the target's own values.
basis.requirement: A recovery of instance (0,0) must not replace with a different value the value that the collected prepare replies report as accepted or pre-accepted; the recovering coordinator adopts the value carried at the highest value ballot among the replies (including its own state) and re-proposes that value if it must restart phase 1.
basis.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's own adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313) and startRecoveryForInstance's construction of its self reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1142-1168), not the client or the environment: the leader's crash after broadcasting Accept is a permitted failure, and the value X was accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3 in the executed scenario.

comparisons.description: The command the recovery proposes for instance (0,0) equals the PUT carried by the prepare reply with the highest value ballot (the quorum-held value X); violated when the recovered PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although quorum_reply_command_op is 1.

A replica that held X after the Accept phase still holds X once the recovered proposal has run to quiescence; violated when the live holder ends up with the NOOP (cmd_op 0) because the recovered PreAccept overwrote its command.

experiments.revision_reason: Corrected observation identity fields so admission events and result events share the comparison identity: prepare_reply now reports the acceptor both as 'from' and as 'replica'; recovery_proposal is emitted once per recovery with a recipients list instead of once per recipient, removing the 'to' identity field that no admission event carried. Message flow, ballots, handlers and the executed scenario are unchanged.

scope.description: Discriminating control for the same 5-replica (F=2) harness and the same message schedule as the value-adoption experiment, with one change: the instance (0,0) recovery is driven by replica 2, which holds the accepted command X (PREACCEPTED_EQ with Cmds X at value ballot 0) rather than by a replica that holds only the accepted coordinates. Everything else is unchanged: the conflicting premise at replica 1, the leader's non-equal pre-accept phase, the Accept broadcast at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3, and the crash of replicas 1 and 0 after the broadcast.
assumptions: Same construction, row sizing, crash model and transport boundary as the value-adoption experiment: in-process replicas with the package's own handlers, marshaled RPC structs decoded per delivery, FIFO per link, no delivery to crashed replicas.
The recovering replica's own self reply carries the real Status (PREACCEPTED_EQ) and Command (X) because it pre-accepted the value; the harness does not supply or alter that state.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no recovery timer loop, no master/BeTheLeader designation.

basis.prefix: The harness runs the shared scenario function with recoverer = 2: proposal of X at replica 0, non-equal pre-accept reply from replica 1 followed by its failure, Accept at ballot 0 delivered to replicas 2 and 3, failure of replica 0 after the broadcast, then startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at replica 2 and completion of the quiescent exchange through the target's own handlers.
basis.requirement: A recovery must preserve the value that the recovering replica itself holds at its value ballot: if the coordinator's own reply carries a command, the recovery's phase-1 restart proposes that command rather than a NOOP, and the instance completes with that command.
basis.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's adoption loop and sub-case dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313) together with startRecoveryForInstance's self reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1142-1168): the crash pattern is identical to the value-adoption experiment, so only the coordinator's own knowledge of the value differs.

comparisons.description: The recovery driven by the replica that holds X re-proposes X (cmd_op 1) even though no remote reply carries a command; expected to hold, establishing that the value loss in the value-adoption experiment comes from the coordinator lacking the value rather than from the crash pattern.
The coordinator that held X still holds X after the recovered proposal ran to quiescence; expected to hold.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) built and driven as in the value-adoption harness (in-process replicas with the package's own handlers and marshaled RPC structs, FIFO delivery, no delivery to crashed replicas). Scenario: replica 1 holds a conflicting command so the owner's pre-accept replies are not equal; owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0) at ballot 0, enters the Accept phase and broadcasts Accept to replicas 1 and 2 (their AcceptReplies are left in flight, i.e. the owner is slow); replica 2 then recovers the same instance at its own ballot 7, so replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4 join ballot 7 and record bal 7, and replica 2 fails after broadcasting that Prepare; the owner then runs two ordinary startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) attempts (as its executor does after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD), and finally a third attempt after the target's own BeTheLeader handler is invoked on it, followed by completion of the quiescent exchange.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers; InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE, and only instance (0,0) is used.

The owner's AcceptReplies from replicas 1 and 2 are never delivered, modelling a slow owner whose recovery timers on the other replicas fire while the replies are in flight; the recovery of an instance whose owner is slow is a normal EPaxos event.
Replica 2's failure is modelled as: no further message is delivered to it, its queue is discarded and every replica's Alive flag for it is cleared.
Replica 1's conflicting command comes from a real startPhase1 whose auxiliary broadcast is discarded; only its local conflict state is used.
IsLeader is set through the target's own BeTheLeader handler, the same RPC the master invokes, and no production logic is modified.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

basis.prefix: The harness drives the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path for the owner, injects the higher-ballot Prepare of replica 2 through handlePrepare at replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4, then calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at the owner three times, delivering every emitted Prepare to the peers' handlePrepare and every PrepareReply back to the owner, and recording the owner's tried ballot, the peers' stored ballots, the appended reply count and any follow-up message. Between attempts 2 and 3 it invokes replica 0's own BeTheLeader handler.
basis.requirement: Recovery authority must be acquirable by the replica that runs the recovery: each recovery attempt must either produce a matching-ballot prepare quorum so that a sub-case is dispatched, or the next attempt at the same instance must use a ballot above the ballots the answering quorum reports, so that a stalled instance can still be recovered.
basis.responsibility: The target's own ballot policy and nack handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 makeBallot, epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235 handlePrepareReply), not the environment or a caller: the peers answer honestly with the ballot they stored, and the repeated attempts are the executor's own retry path (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

comparisons.description: Without the designated-leader authority, a recovery attempt at an instance whose answering quorum reports a higher stored ballot still reaches SlowQuorumSize appended replies and dispatches a sub-case; violated when appended_replies stays 1 and no follow-up message is emitted.

The retry ballot exceeds the ballot the peers already stored, so the retry can act on the instance; violated when tried_ballot stays at 0 while stored_bal_before_attempt is 7 on both repeated attempts.
Control: after the target's own BeTheLeader handler runs, the attempt uses a ballot above the stored one and the sub-case dispatch happens; expected to hold.
Control outcome: with the authority granted, the owner's recovery completes the instance (status COMMITTED) and keeps the accepted command X; expected to hold.

inst.lb = r.newLeaderBookkeepingDefault()
	lb := inst.lb
	lb.clientProposals = proposals
	lb.ballot = inst.vbal
	lb.seq = inst.Seq
	lb.cmds = inst.Cmds
	lb.deps = inst.Deps
	lb.status = inst.Status
	r.makeBallot(replica, instance)

	inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	preply := &PrepareReply{
		r.Id,
		replica,
		instance,
		inst.bal,
		inst.vbal,
		inst.Status,
		inst.Cmds,
		inst.Seq,
		inst.Deps}

	lb.prepareReplies = append(lb.prepareReplies, preply)
	lb.leaderResponded = r.Id == replica

	r.bcastPrepare(replica, instance)

result.summary: Requested execution of a sharper variant probe and recorded a second mechanism it exposed locally. In the new scenario the owner commits X and fails after its Commit reaches only one live peer, so replica 2 holds X COMMITTED while replica 3 recovers the same instance holding no command. Local native feedback shows the recovery proposing the NOOP although replica 2's prepare reply carried X with status COMMITTED, and then stalling: adopting that COMMITTED status into lb.status makes the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 discard replica 4's reply, so the restarted phase-1 proposal never reaches its fast quorum and replica 3's instance stays pre-accepted with no accept or commit emitted. That mechanism is recorded as a new behavior with a new source range (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895) and a new active question about whether the stall repeats identically on the executor's retry, with the two comparisons (recovery proposes the quorum-reported value; the recovering replica reaches a decided state) declared for the controller's receipt. This turn's unfinished work: the interpretation of that receipt and confirmation that the observed incompleteness is the target's status-guard interaction rather than harness scheduling.

investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.
InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE (10M); only instances 0..2 are used, so no code path indexes beyond the allocated row.

The auxiliary broadcast of replica 1's conflicting proposal is discarded; only its local conflict state (conflicts[2][key 1]) is used as the premise that makes the leader's pre-accept reply non-equal and therefore forces the Accept phase.

Crashes are modelled as: the replica stops consuming messages, no further message is delivered to it, and every other replica's Alive flag for it is cleared, matching the target's mechanism for deciding broadcast recipients.
Replica 3's recovery is invoked through startRecoveryForInstance, the same function the target's executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD.
excluded: No client connection path, no execution of the state machine, no recovery timer loop, and no master/BeTheLeader designation (IsLeader stays false, as epaxos.New sets it).

basis.prefix: The harness builds five in-process replicas, injects the conflicting premise at replica 1, runs replica 0's proposal of X through the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, crashes replicas 1 and 0, then calls replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers the resulting Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through the package's own handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply. Every outgoing message is decoded from the bytes SendMsg flushed, so message content, ballot fields and commands are the target's own values.
basis.requirement: A recovery of instance (0,0) must not replace with a different value the value that the collected prepare replies report as accepted or pre-accepted; the recovering coordinator adopts the value carried at the highest value ballot among the replies (including its own state) and re-proposes that value if it must restart phase 1.
basis.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's own adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313) and startRecoveryForInstance's construction of its self reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1142-1168), not the client or the environment: the leader's crash after broadcasting Accept is a permitted failure, and the value X was accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3 in the executed scenario.

comparisons.description: The command the recovery proposes for instance (0,0) equals the PUT carried by the prepare reply with the highest value ballot (the quorum-held value X); violated when the recovered PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although quorum_reply_command_op is 1.

A replica that held X after the Accept phase still holds X once the recovered proposal has run to quiescence; violated when the live holder ends up with the NOOP (cmd_op 0) because the recovered PreAccept overwrote its command.

scope.description: Discriminating control for the same 5-replica (F=2) harness and the same message schedule as the value-adoption experiment, with one change: the instance (0,0) recovery is driven by replica 2, which holds the accepted command X (PREACCEPTED_EQ with Cmds X at value ballot 0) rather than by a replica that holds only the accepted coordinates. Everything else is unchanged: the conflicting premise at replica 1, the leader's non-equal pre-accept phase, the Accept broadcast at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3, and the crash of replicas 1 and 0 after the broadcast.
assumptions: Same construction, row sizing, crash model and transport boundary as the value-adoption experiment: in-process replicas with the package's own handlers, marshaled RPC structs decoded per delivery, FIFO per link, no delivery to crashed replicas.
The recovering replica's own self reply carries the real Status (PREACCEPTED_EQ) and Command (X) because it pre-accepted the value; the harness does not supply or alter that state.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no recovery timer loop, no master/BeTheLeader designation.

basis.prefix: The harness runs the shared scenario function with recoverer = 2: proposal of X at replica 0, non-equal pre-accept reply from replica 1 followed by its failure, Accept at ballot 0 delivered to replicas 2 and 3, failure of replica 0 after the broadcast, then startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at replica 2 and completion of the quiescent exchange through the target's own handlers.

comparisons.description: The recovery driven by the replica that holds X re-proposes X (cmd_op 1) even though no remote reply carries a command; expected to hold, establishing that the value loss in the value-adoption experiment comes from the coordinator lacking the value rather than from the crash pattern.
The coordinator that held X still holds X after the recovered proposal ran to quiescence; expected to hold.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) built and driven as in the value-adoption harness (in-process replicas with the package's own handlers and marshaled RPC structs, FIFO delivery, no delivery to crashed replicas). Scenario: replica 1 holds a conflicting command so the owner's pre-accept replies are not equal; owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0) at ballot 0, enters the Accept phase and broadcasts Accept to replicas 1 and 2 (their AcceptReplies are left in flight, i.e. the owner is slow); replica 2 then recovers the same instance at its own ballot 7, so replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4 join ballot 7 and record bal 7, and replica 2 fails after broadcasting that Prepare; the owner then runs two ordinary startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) attempts (as its executor does after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD), and finally a third attempt after the target's own BeTheLeader handler is invoked on it, followed by completion of the quiescent exchange.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers; InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE, and only instance (0,0) is used.

The owner's AcceptReplies from replicas 1 and 2 are never delivered, modelling a slow owner whose recovery timers on the other replicas fire while the replies are in flight; the recovery of an instance whose owner is slow is a normal EPaxos event.
Replica 2's failure is modelled as: no further message is delivered to it, its queue is discarded and every replica's Alive flag for it is cleared.
Replica 1's conflicting command comes from a real startPhase1 whose auxiliary broadcast is discarded; only its local conflict state is used.
IsLeader is set through the target's own BeTheLeader handler, the same RPC the master invokes, and no production logic is modified.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

basis.prefix: The harness drives the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path for the owner, injects the higher-ballot Prepare of replica 2 through handlePrepare at replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4, then calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) at the owner three times, delivering every emitted Prepare to the peers' handlePrepare and every PrepareReply back to the owner, and recording the owner's tried ballot, the peers' stored ballots, the appended reply count and any follow-up message. Between attempts 2 and 3 it invokes replica 0's own BeTheLeader handler.
basis.requirement: Recovery authority must be acquirable by the replica that runs the recovery: each recovery attempt must either produce a matching-ballot prepare quorum so that a sub-case is dispatched, or the next attempt at the same instance must use a ballot above the ballots the answering quorum reports, so that a stalled instance can still be recovered.
basis.responsibility: The target's own ballot policy and nack handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 makeBallot, epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235 handlePrepareReply), not the environment or a caller: the peers answer honestly with the ballot they stored, and the repeated attempts are the executor's own retry path (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417).

comparisons.description: Without the designated-leader authority, a recovery attempt at an instance whose answering quorum reports a higher stored ballot still reaches SlowQuorumSize appended replies and dispatches a sub-case; violated when appended_replies stays 1 and no follow-up message is emitted.

The retry ballot exceeds the ballot the peers already stored, so the retry can act on the instance; violated when tried_ballot stays at 0 while stored_bal_before_attempt is 7 on both repeated attempts.

Control outcome: with the authority granted, the owner's recovery completes the instance (status COMMITTED) and keeps the accepted command X; expected to hold.

scope.description: Variant of the value-adoption harness that first lets the instance owner commit the value X and then fail, so that the same instance is recovered by a replica that holds no command while another live replica holds X committed. The owner's Commit reaching only replica 2 models the owner failing immediately after the first Commit of its broadcast, which is a permitted crash point.
No production logic is modified; the authority and crash flags are set only through the target's own fields and handlers.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

basis.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's adoption of a reply's Status into lb.status together with the guard that discards later replies (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895) and its value adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313); the peer's report of COMMITTED is the target's own honest reply.

comparisons.description: The value the recovery proposes does not replace the value the quorum reports; violated when the recovery's PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although a reply carried X with status COMMITTED.

The recovering replica's own instance reaches a decided state after the recovered proposal; violated when it remains in a pre-accept state because the adopted COMMITTED status made the leader discard the replies it needed.
